class: single-listener blinded informal check by the first author (Gabriel Bibbó); descriptive; N=1; NOT the frozen six-listener panel; no gate; cannot change any verdict

design.blinding: opaque clip ids; key sealed before listening

block_A_content_10p24s.reading: the 83 %-pruned checkpoint's near-floor CLAP is mostly DEGENERATE audio (changing noise with compression-like artefacts, 'galactic' textures), not plausible audio that misses the caption; P+FT is recognisable on 7/8 and matches on 4/8. Caveat from the listener: wind-in-microphone-like distortion is heard as 'realistic', which inflates 'recognisable' for noise-like outputs

3.84s.reading: at 3.84 s the ear does NOT confirm the CLAP short-duration gain (R_short +0.085): both outputs mostly judged noise, weak preference for P

10.24s.reading: at 10.24 s the recovery gain is audible: P+FT preferred 6/8 with full confidence in 6/8; the 2 exceptions are prompts where P+FT was near-silent or noise

block_B_duration_pairs.reading: the audible margin grows with duration (0/8 -> 6/8), consistent in direction with the CLAP interaction J; the ear places the short-duration gain lower than CLAP does

block_C_music_pairs_10p24s.reading: CLAP's null on music (R_music ~ 0, both near chance) hides an audible difference: P+FT is clearly more MUSICAL (5/8 'music', 8/8 preferred) while neither follows the long MusicCaps captions (means 1.4 / 2.5). Musicality without caption alignment is invisible to a text-audio scorer

listener_free_text: see artifacts/icassp_gate0/author_listening/mis_respuestas.md (gitignored) — concerns: distortion that resembles wind-in-mic reads as realistic; the music captions are too long/specific for 10 s clips and may make every system look bad
prompt_provenance_note: AudioCaps-test prompts selected by seeded hash from the frozen 192-prompt manifest, no content filtering (xsev_select_audiocaps.py); music captions are MusicCaps hip-hop/rap, keyword-filtered only (xsev_select_music.py); the listening subset is a seeded random draw. Nothing was chosen for difficulty
